nodes.label: Graphify Build Manifest Inclusion Patterns
nodes.rationale: The path filters explicitly list graphify-out/.graphify_build.json and the corresponding frontend and backend paths after the directory exclusions.

nodes.label: Graphify Output Directory Exclusion Patterns
nodes.rationale: The three negative path filters target graphify-out/** at the root, in src/main/web-static and in src/main/go; they do not exclude the explicitly listed build-manifest paths that follow.

nodes.label: Vendored Graphify Skill Exclusion Pattern
nodes.rationale: The negative path filter targets .agents/skills/graphify/**.

nodes.label: Graphify Compatibility and SQL Extraction Limits
nodes.norm_label: graphify compatibility and sql extraction limits
nodes.rationale: Keep installed Graphify compatible with the vendored skill; SQL re-extraction needs the optional graphifyy[sql] extra, and the 0.9.64 parser does not identify every migration statement.

nodes.label: Seven Reviewed SQL Host-Agent Semantic Supplements
nodes.norm_label: seven reviewed sql host-agent semantic supplements
nodes.rationale: Seven SQL migration parser gaps have reviewed host-agent semantic supplements; this file does not identify the affected statements.

nodes.label: Graphify-First Codebase Navigation
nodes.rationale: Use the graph for the source area being investigated; never substitute the remainder graph for a missing module graph, and verify cross-module boundaries against source.

nodes.label: Host-Agent Semantic Chunk Validation
nodes.rationale: Before merging, validate chunk source membership, relationship schema and provenance; for the remainder enumerate allowed files using the tracked root exclusions before dispatch.

nodes.label: Post-Root-Update Graph Refresh and Integrity Gate
nodes.norm_label: post-root-update graph refresh and integrity gate
nodes.rationale: After SQL stub cleanup, run graphify cluster-only "$PWD" --no-label, then python3 src/test/graphify-graphs.py.

nodes.label: Root Exclusion-Aware Semantic Refresh
nodes.rationale: The remainder corpus excludes frontend and backend modules; avoid skill root-wide detection/rebuild and /graphify --update because those instructions ignore tracked root exclusions. Merge reviewed chunks via native scoped Graphify APIs.

nodes.label: Post-Root-Update SQL Stub Cleanup
nodes.rationale: After a root Graphify update, run src/ext/graphify/prune-sql-stubs.py using Graphify's Python interpreter; the cleanup refuses unknown disconnected nodes.

nodes.label: Scoped Native Graphify AST Update
nodes.rationale: Update each affected scope; use absolute module scan roots because relative module paths in Graphify 0.9.64 changed node source paths and subsequently lost semantic nodes. The root update respects tracked module exclusions and preserves, but does not refresh, semantic content.

nodes.label: Three-Scope Graph Selection
nodes.rationale: Select by source area rather than working directory; query relevant graphs independently for cross-module questions.

nodes.label: Scoped Semantic Extraction and Cluster Refresh
nodes.norm_label: scoped semantic extraction and cluster refresh
nodes.rationale: For changed semantic sources, extract at the absolute scope path and run cluster-only --no-label; module-assisted extraction must stay inside that module.

nodes.label: Host-Agent Semantic Provenance
nodes.rationale: Set _origin to semantic and source_location to null when merging; L-shaped locations without an origin can be interpreted as AST and leave stale semantic nodes.

nodes.label: chromedp with Go Testing
nodes.rationale: Excluded as primary because it is Chromium-only, lacks an integrated E2E runner and diagnostics workflow, carries high harness cost, and had failing retained upstream CI runs.

nodes.label: CodeceptJS
nodes.rationale: A viable but non-primary abstraction over Playwright/WebDriver/Puppeteer; its recorder/helper model and ESM transition add synchronization and migration layers.

nodes.label: Cucumber.js with Playwright or Playwright-BDD
nodes.rationale: Technically capable through Playwright, but justified only when stakeholders actively review Gherkin; otherwise generated tests and step indirection add cost without value.

nodes.label: Cypress
nodes.rationale: Cypress is actively maintained and adopted, but its command queue, weaker WebKit support, Cloud-dependent native load balancing, and additional lifecycle work reduce fit relative to direct Playwright.

nodes.label: Grafana k6 Browser
nodes.rationale: Excluded as primary because it is Chromium-only, lacks browser download support and a fixture-aware E2E runner, but remains useful for supplementary performance and Web Vitals journeys.

nodes.label: Nightwatch.js
nodes.rationale: A viable but non-primary alternative due to low recent activity, Selenium binding lag, stale CI guidance, and substantial custom harness work.

nodes.label: Playwright Test
nodes.rationale: Direct Playwright provides three managed engines, HTMX-friendly locators, isolated contexts, integrated retries, traces, reports, API/network controls, and a low-to-moderate project-specific harness burden; the empirical repository spike was not completed.

nodes.label: Puppeteer with Vitest or Jest
nodes.rationale: Actively maintained and flexible, but lacks WebKit/Safari, an integrated download object, web-first assertion workflow, server lifecycle, and automatic E2E failure bundles.

nodes.label: Robot Framework Browser
nodes.rationale: A viable non-primary option for business-readable keyword suites; direct Playwright better matches this Go/TypeScript repository and avoids a Python/Robot DSL layer.

nodes.label: Rod with Go Testing
nodes.rationale: Excluded as primary because its final release and guaranteed Chromium/CDP baseline are from 2024, coverage is Chromium-only, and maintenance is highly concentrated.

nodes.label: Selenium WebDriver with JavaScript
nodes.rationale: Retained as the mature standards-based baseline, but high custom harness and diagnostics burden makes it a viable alternative rather than the leading recommendation.

nodes.label: TestCafe
nodes.rationale: Current use remains material, but declining adoption, slow feature cadence, stale documentation, an archived GitHub Action, and incomplete native automation create selection risk.

nodes.label: Testplane
nodes.rationale: A viable alternative with strong visual regression, retries, sharding, and diagnosis, but a smaller independent ecosystem and untested project gates prevent default selection.

nodes.label: WebdriverIO
nodes.rationale: Classified as a viable alternative, pending a spike for Node 24, TypeScript 6, HTMX replacement, database reset, downloads, and current BiDi reliability.

nodes.label: Asset Allocation Strategy
nodes.rationale: The project treats allocation as a long-term, emotionally disciplined plan that exploits cyclic markets while emphasizing diversification, barbell strategies, and tail-risk hedging.

nodes.label: Fractal Portfolio Hierarchy
nodes.rationale: Assets form the lowest level and can be repeatedly grouped by model-defined criteria into higher levels.

nodes.label: Renovate Runtime Coordination
nodes.rationale: Dependabot ignores Node, Playwright, and Node type references that Renovate must update as coordinated version sets.

nodes.label: Go and Air Image Version Coordination
nodes.norm_label: go and air image version coordination
nodes.rationale: Keep the Go language version aligned with the latest available cosmtrek/air image and bump them together.

nodes.label: Application Node.js LTS Runtime Coordination
nodes.rationale: The same exact LTS Node.js version is required in .nvmrc, frontend Dockerfile and monolith frontend build stage; Renovate exclusively updates these references, while Dependabot ignores the node Docker dependency.

nodes.label: Playwright and E2E Node Type Major Alignment
nodes.norm_label: playwright and e2e node type major alignment
nodes.rationale: The Playwright image has its own Node.js runtime; align its major with E2E @types/node rather than the application Node.js runtime.

nodes.label: Production Monolith
nodes.rationale: Production packages the Go backend and immutable Parcel distribution in one image so Gin serves the API and frontend from one process and origin.

nodes.label: Coordinated Playwright Updates
nodes.rationale: The npm package, lockfile packages, and Playwright Docker image must remain on one exact version, with Renovate coordinating them.

nodes.label: Disposable PostgreSQL Isolation
nodes.rationale: Every attempt truncates public base tables before and after execution, and the suite removes the named PostgreSQL volume as the final boundary.

nodes.label: Existing Graph Fast Path
nodes.rationale: Natural-language codebase questions use the existing graph immediately rather than rebuilding or broadly rescanning the corpus.

nodes.label: Graphify Honesty Rules
nodes.rationale: Graphify must not invent edges, skip corpus warnings, hide token cost or cohesion, or silently render very large graphs.

nodes.label: asset.external_data migration retrieval evidence
nodes.rationale: The remainder 'asset.external_data' query reached 134 nodes and displayed 30, starting with the host-agent concept for the JSONB column added by migration 14; results were truncated and included unrelated E2E nodes, so a path-qualified lookup remains necessary for precise evidence.

nodes.label: Build configuration file retrieval miss
nodes.rationale: The post-refresh remainder 'graphify build configuration' query reached 30 nodes including scoped-configuration guidance, but no .graphify_build.json file node. The tracked dotfiles are not indexed; read all three directly to learn their actual contents, even when a semantic guide points toward them.

nodes.label: Code-only graph bootstrap
nodes.rationale: A missing graph can be bootstrapped from its code corpus, but this does not extract a semantic layer for templates or documents.

nodes.label: Committed graph integrity check
nodes.rationale: Checks graph scope membership, portable paths, endpoints, hyperedges, report metadata, connected source-less references, and representative code, template, Docker, E2E, and Flyway SQL coverage. A migration file node alone is not content coverage; host-agent supplements are semantic nodes, not parsed SQL schema.

nodes.label: Operator-configured Graphify semantic backend
nodes.rationale: Native semantic extraction requires an operator-configured, Graphify-supported backend and fails explicitly if it is missing; Graphify's native CLI has no OpenCode backend.

nodes.label: Disposable Graphify integration fixture
nodes.rationale: The integration test runs native Graphify on a disposable small repository with copies of tracked configurations; a separate OpenCode host-agent fixture exercised HTML and Markdown refresh in all three scopes. These are validation fixtures, not a production OpenCode backend.

nodes.label: Explicit --graph selection
nodes.rationale: Choose a graph explicitly for queries and path lookups rather than relying on a merged graph or treating the remainder graph as a module fallback.

nodes.label: Narrow fail-closed Flyway SQL stub repair
nodes.norm_label: narrow fail-closed flyway sql stub repair
nodes.rationale: After a root update, run src/ext/graphify/prune-sql-stubs.py using Graphify's own Python interpreter, regenerate the root report with cluster-only, and run the graph integrity check. The repair refuses to write if any disconnected source-less node is not an unowned Flyway SQL AST stub; it is a Graphify 0.9.64 parser workaround, not a general update wrapper, and its need must be reassessed on parser upgrades.

nodes.label: Host-agent token usage reporting limit
nodes.rationale: OpenCode-assisted extraction consumes host-agent tokens, but generated chunks do not report reliable token usage; zero CLI extraction tokens in Graphify's report do not measure host-agent cost.

nodes.label: Native scoped Graphify AST updates
nodes.rationale: Run Graphify update independently for each affected scope; AST updates alone do not refresh changed templates, documents, or images.

nodes.label: OpenCode host-agent semantic refresh
nodes.rationale: OpenCode can execute the generated skill as host agent, but reviewed semantic chunks are merged through Graphify's library rather than through a nonexistent native OpenCode backend; module skills start inside their respective modules.

nodes.label: Partial Flyway SQL statement coverage
nodes.rationale: The SQL AST parser contributes only file nodes for seven of fourteen Flyway migrations. After reviewed semantic supplementation, every Flyway migration has a content node, but not every SQL statement is parsed; host-agent concepts are not parsed SQL schema.

nodes.label: Post-refresh Flyway migration retrieval evidence
nodes.rationale: After SQL and host-agent semantic refresh, 'flyway migrations' in the remainder reached 27 nodes without displaying a specific SQL table; 'migration allocation_plan' reached 33 and displayed 19, including migration 5/6 constraints and migration 12's rename, but truncated before migration 1's table. A path-qualified explain resolved migration 1's allocation_plan at line 102 and its references.

nodes.label: Recurring disconnected Flyway SQL AST stubs
nodes.norm_label: recurring disconnected flyway sql ast stubs
nodes.rationale: Graphify 0.9.64 with its SQL parser installed can add six disconnected Flyway SQL stubs after each remainder update. This is a parser artifact, not evidence that all migration statements were indexed.

nodes.label: Remainder-only semantic candidate detection
nodes.rationale: Enumerate remainder semantic candidates using the root build configuration's excludes and gitignore, then verify that no frontend or backend module file is dispatched; the skill's default root-wide detection does not apply these exclusions.

nodes.label: Scoped .graphify_build.json configurations
nodes.rationale: The tracked configurations persist each graph's corpus boundary; the root configuration excludes both application module trees without using a root .graphifyignore that would also affect module scans.

nodes.label: Scoped Graphify retrieval comparison
nodes.rationale: Dated BFS-depth-2 queries with a 1,200-token budget show scoped results but broad queries may truncate or exceed the budget. The remainder comparison was repeated after SQL and host-agent semantic refresh; observed results are evidence, not a guarantee of complete source or statement retrieval.

nodes.label: Semantic provenance normalization
nodes.rationale: Review chunks against the extraction schema, mark _origin as semantic and source_location as null before build_merge; an AST-shaped L1-L3 agent location without semantic origin can leave stale nodes after refresh.

nodes.label: Semantic source refresh
nodes.rationale: Changed HTML/HTMX templates, documents, and images require semantic extraction in addition to a local AST update.

nodes.label: Seven Flyway migration semantic supplements
nodes.rationale: OpenCode-assisted extraction added reviewed, source-attributed concepts and relationships for the seven migrations whose SQL AST extraction produced only file nodes. The supplement provides partial content coverage, not complete parsing or a replacement SQL parser.

nodes.label: Source-verified frontend-to-backend asset route
nodes.rationale: The frontend asset template's hx-get=/api/asset and the backend asset controller's /api/asset registration establish the HTTP boundary from inspected source, not from a cross-graph inferred link.

nodes.label: Disconnected source-less reference cleanup
nodes.rationale: An initial graph cleanup removed 75 unconnected source-less references, including six SQL stubs; six SQL stubs recur on later root updates, and the integrity check rejects all disconnected source-less nodes.

nodes.label: Graphify tree_sitter_sql optional parser
nodes.rationale: The graphifyy[sql]==0.9.64 extra enabled attributed SQL file nodes on a remainder rebuild; a fresh checkout needs the compatible extra to rebuild or refresh SQL nodes.

nodes.label: Absolute module scan paths
nodes.rationale: With Graphify 0.9.64, repository-relative module paths were observed to prefix graph source paths and cause a later update to prune semantic nodes; absolute module scan paths preserve module-relative graph source paths.

nodes.label: Graph revision stamp freshness limit
nodes.rationale: A graph's built_at_commit describes its most recent build, not the independent freshness of every preserved semantic node; the extraction-time Git revision does not prove that uncommitted host-agent changes were absent.

nodes.label: Three scoped Graphify graphs
nodes.rationale: Separating frontend, backend, and remainder graphs prevents attributed sources from unrelated modules appearing in scoped query results; the root graph is not a fallback for module sources.

nodes.norm_label: actual vs planned market value comparison

nodes.label: Directional Divergence Bars
nodes.rationale: Uses compact striped bars and contrasting colors to make divergence direction and relative magnitude scannable.

nodes.label: Hierarchical Asset Allocation Breakdown
nodes.rationale: Groups individual holdings beneath Bonds and Stocks so aggregate and constituent allocation drift can be inspected together.

nodes.label: Automatic Non-Draft CodeRabbit Review Policy
nodes.rationale: The configuration enables auto_review, disables drafts, and sets assertive review profile, en-US language and high-level summaries.

nodes.label: AI-Generated Code Documentation and Authorship
nodes.rationale: Document generated code at module, entity and method levels using language conventions, record agent authorship on touched code, and give detailed public API usage.

nodes.label: Atomic Persistence-Verified E2E Testing
nodes.rationale: Tests use only their own scope; create fixtures directly in the database, assert modifications on the persistence layer, and avoid production test hooks unless unavoidable.

nodes.label: Problem-Domain Literacy
nodes.rationale: Contributors should understand the real-world problem through direct experience, documentation, questions, and domain expertise.

nodes.label: Weighted Project Fit Score
nodes.rationale: The score weights application fit at 30%, maintenance 20%, reliability and adoption 15% each, CI experience 10%, and diagnostics plus cost/risk 5% each.
